title: Attack, capture and defend

card.idea: A piece attacks every square it could move to. Capturing means landing on an enemy piece and lifting it off the board. A piece is defended when a friendly piece could take back on that square.

explain.text: The rook on c5 attacks the bishop on c8 and the knight on g5. Attacking simply means it could move there next turn and take.
Defended means a friend can take back. The pawn on b3 defends the knight on c4. The king on e1 defends the rook on d1. The pawn on b3 has nobody behind it.

challenges.prompt: Tap every black piece the white rook attacks.
Tap every white piece that is defended.

hints.text: Two of the three are defended. The pawn on b3 is the odd one out.

challenges.prompt: The rook takes the pawn on e5. Is that safe?
reasons: The knight on d7 would take back.
The king on g8 would take back.

hints.text: The king on g8 is three squares away from e5, so it is not the one to worry about.

challenges.prompt: Capture the black piece that nothing defends.

wrong.Rd4: The knight on c5 is defended by the bishop on d5. Take the defender instead.

challenges.reason: Nothing guards d5, so the rook wins a whole bishop.

challenges.prompt: The knight can take something. Take the piece nothing defends.
challenges.reason: No black piece can take back on e6, so the rook is free.
The pawn takes the bishop on b3 and nothing takes back.

takeaway: Attacked means a piece could take it. Defended means a friend would take back.
